security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown links, fenced code blocks, inline command examples, and expected Claude skill installation paths. Confirmed risk remains in setup blocks that run package managers, local scripts, and broad file rewrite commands. No evidence found of obfuscated payloads or prompt-injection language.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before package installs, script execution, server starts, and broad file rewrites.
Document why ~/.claude/skills/genesis is required, and avoid using hidden home paths for anything except installed skill assets.
Include the referenced templates and references directories, or remove commands that depend on unavailable files.

content.user_title: Create Full Stack Starters with Genesis
content.value_statement: Starting new web, backend, or miniapp projects requires many repeated setup steps. Genesis provides guided workflows for React, FastAPI, Go Gin, Taro, landing pages, and motion upgrades.
actual_capabilities: Guides users through selecting React, FastAPI, Go Gin, or Taro project setup.
Documents Mode A template copy commands for web, Python, Go, and miniapp projects.
References Mode B generation paths for supported stacks.
Describes landing page generation for existing React projects.
Describes React motion enhancement using Framer Motion concepts.
Lists installation and verification commands for Claude Code skill setup.
limitations: The scanned package does not include the referenced templates or references directories.
Template copy commands assume installation at ~/.claude/skills/genesis.
Several flows run package managers and local servers after copying files.
It does not provide project-specific business logic or deployment infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Start a React Product Interface
use_cases.description: Create a guided React starter workflow with Vite, TailwindCSS, shadcn/ui, landing page sections, and motion guidance.

use_cases.title: Create an API Starter
use_cases.description: Prepare a FastAPI or Go Gin backend workflow with documented setup commands, module naming steps, and local run instructions.

use_cases.title: Plan a Cross-Platform Miniapp
use_cases.description: Use the Taro workflow to outline setup for WeChat, Alipay, Douyin, and H5 targets.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic React Starter
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a React project named customer-portal. Ask me for Mode A or Mode B before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Build a FastAPI Service
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a FastAPI backend named orders-api in ./services/orders. Use Mode B and explain each step before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Landing Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a landing page for the current React project using the Genesis section structure and motion guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Go API Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Go Gin API and adjust module names across Go files. List every command before running it.

output_examples.input: Create a React project named customer-portal.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for a setup mode, confirms the target directory, then prepares a React starter workflow with install and run steps.

output_examples.input: Generate a landing page for my current React app.
output: A section plan for hero, features, social proof, pricing, and FAQ.
Motion and accessibility notes for each section.

output_examples.input: Create a Go Gin backend for an internal API.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms the project name, target directory, and setup mode, then outlines file rewrite and local run steps.

best_practices: Confirm project type, name, target directory, and setup mode before starting.
Review package manager commands and local scripts before allowing execution.
Verify generated projects in a disposable directory before moving them into production.
anti_patterns: Running setup in a directory that already contains important files.
Assuming referenced templates exist without checking the installed skill contents.
Allowing dependency installation or local servers without reviewing package scripts.

faq.question: Which stacks does Genesis cover?
faq.answer: It covers React, FastAPI, Go Gin, Taro miniapps, landing pages, and React motion upgrades.

faq.question: Does this package include templates?
faq.answer: The scanned package does not include templates or references. The instructions assume they exist in the installed skill path.

faq.question: Can it work without running commands?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask the assistant to explain the plan and wait for approval before executing setup commands.

faq.question: Does it support Codex?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Is automatic execution recommended?
faq.answer: No. Review package manager commands, local scripts, and target directories before execution.

faq.question: Can it modify existing React apps?
faq.answer: It documents landing page and motion enhancement workflows for existing React projects.
